rules.when: The task is a separate read-only planning assignment: architecture, decomposition, acceptance criteria, or a design decision needed before implementation. It is not routine task coordination or implementation from an accepted plan.
rules.why: High reasoning belongs in bounded planning. Return a concise plan and stop before implementation.

rules.when: The task is narrow read-only reconnaissance, file gathering, a mechanical edit, formatting, a targeted rename, or another straightforward operation with clear acceptance criteria.
rules.why: Use the requested GPT-6 Luna worker at extra-high reasoning for routine work too. Do not silently substitute a low-effort or different-model worker.

rules.when: The task is scoped implementation or straightforward tests from a sufficiently clear accepted plan, without unresolved architecture. Execution workers use the requested GPT-6 Luna extra-high profile.
rules.why: Implementation uses GPT-6 Luna with explicit xhigh reasoning after planning has removed architectural ambiguity.

rules.when: The task is an additional independent review explicitly requested or justified by the change, ambiguous debugging, or implementation that the manager has explicitly escalated after the execution worker attempt was inadequate. Routine acceptance code review is performed by the medium-reasoning manager itself and is not a worker assignment. Unresolved architectural planning decisions belong to the planning rule.
rules.why: Use medium reasoning for an additional review or a demonstrated need. An extra reviewer assists rather than replaces the manager's personal code review; return architectural uncertainty to the high-tier planner.
